correctness.rationale: Conjugation averaging over matched-pair permutations and part interchange is feasible and operator-norm nonincreasing. The four exact invariant subspaces exhaust all 2m dimensions and yield SLEM max(|2c-1|,c+|a-b|). Two globally valid crossing-affine lower bounds meet the two explicitly feasible designs on the opposite sides of a*=2/(3m); projection gives the exact interval optimum. Both m=2 and a=0,1 are explicitly included. An exact-Fraction program replays 35,344 checks of eigenvectors, stochasticity, formulas, and finite parameter comparisons; these checks are supplementary to the all-m proof.

evidence: The 2004 and 2009 convex FMMC frameworks cover the optimization algorithmically, but their displayed closed forms are for the uncolored unrestricted bipartite topology.
Jafarizadeh (2010), sections III and V, describes layered K-partite pseudo-distance-regular networks, with full cross-layer adjacency; it does not present matched-partner transition constraints.
broader_coverage.reasoning: General SDP solvability does not imply the stated exact closed-form frontier without solving its particular two-color spectral problem. The 2010 layered topology does not distinguish individual partner links from the remaining cross links; the all-parameter result does not follow as one of its displayed formulas.

value.rationale: Matched communication links form a natural fixed perfect-matching resource in symmetric bipartite load balancing and Markov mixing. The exact all-size all-capacity SLEM response is not an arbitrary one-off graph calculation: the rate is a nontrivial two-sided affine envelope, the optimal matched probability is sharply 2/(3m), and deficient/excessive matched capacity incur distinct exact penalties. The interval theorem solves arbitrary heterogeneous per-link bounds with a single realizable uniform design, avoiding a separate semidefinite solve. This is a motivated complete classification for one capacity parameter, though it does not claim a general topology theorem.
